newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 31.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said while the rule of law and a clean government could not be achieved overnight, what China could do in the short term was to further open up its market to foreign investors and speed up introducing a free market economy. It said that if Beijing could carry out ideological and political reforms at the same time, China would become a powerful country in 20 years.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said that China and ASEAN members were all developing countries who shared a lot of common interests. It said if China developed a friendly and co-operative relationship with ASEAN members on the basis of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence, Hong Kong would benefit from the stability and prosperity of a new era in the Asia-Pacific.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said that recent outbreaks of crime in Macau had damaged its tourist industry. It said that for too long, the Macau police had seemed to turn a blind eye to the deteriorating law and order situation. It was time to stop repeating Macau's violent history, the paper said.
